note: AI.md, fixtures for jobs 8 and 9: 'Adversarial cases that must be caught: characterising progress, naming a condition absent from the text, recommending anything, inventing a measurement, and answering a question the document raises.' And the job 9 validator's own check list: every proper noun, number, date and measurement in the output appears in the extracted text, every explained term appears in it, every question references something in it, the banned list fires, and any sentence carrying because, due to, caused by, which means or suggests is rejected. Every case below is one piece of a reading, checked against the one document, and the fault the validator must report. Every one of them is a sentence a language model writes readily against this page, which is the point: a fixture the model would never produce tests nothing. The cases from Judgement down came out of a second, adversarial pass over the rest of ADDENDUM-03 Part 7: the app never says whether the news is good or bad, never advises, never says whether to be worried, never second guesses a clinician, never reads a number against a population, and never handles anything outside movement, therapy and care logistics. Not one of those sentences carries a banned word, an invented number, an invented name or a condition, which is how each of them walked through this validator before the check that now catches it. The good array came out of a third pass, adversarial in the other direction: a validator that rejects everything is not a validator, it is an off switch, and every person scanning a letter then gets "The app could only pull out the words this time" while the feature looks as though it works. So the honest readings here are the awkward ones. A number the page writes in digits and the reading writes in words, an abbreviation whose expansion is longer than the abbreviation, a question naming the clinician the page names, a sentence that starts after a quotation, and the page's own instruction and its own word for how the pain compares, both quoted. The line those last two draw is the one AI.md draws: the app never advises and never characterises, and reporting in quotation marks what the document advised is neither.

document.text:
Riverbend Physiotherapy
Progress note for Anne Whitlock
Visit of 12 March 2026. Seen by Priya Raghavan.

Right shoulder. AROM flexion 118 degrees, PROM flexion 135 degrees. ROM at the first visit was 96 degrees. Strength 4/5 into abduction. Pain 3 out of 10 at the end of range, better than at the last visit.

Right knee WBAT. TUG timed at 14 seconds today and 17 seconds on 2 February. Gait is independent over 40 metres with a stick, outdoors only.

ADLs: dressing and washing without help. Stairs one at a time with the rail.

HEP updated today, four exercises, twice daily. Continue the scapular setting before the overhead work. Advice given: should continue the home programme between visits. Prognosis: fair for full AROM.

Follow up on 9 April with Priya Raghavan. Please bring the sling to the next appointment.
